body_markdown:
Swimming banned at Maroubra and Coogee while council prioritises ‘culturally respectful’ approach to remains Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast A whale carcass has forced the closure of two busy swimming and surfing spots after washing up between Coogee and Maroubra beaches in Sydney – but there are no plans to remove it. The whale’s heavily decomposed body was found on Thursday morning at Lurline Bay, a rocky cove surrounded by cliffs in Sydney’s eastern suburbs. (The Guardian Australia)

**Stuff** adds: Residents have been warned of increased shark activity after the carcass was discovered floating close to shore in the eastern suburbs.

**ABC News Australia** adds: Randwick Council has closed Maroubra and Coogee beaches as a precaution, over concerns the carcass may attract sharks.

This digest was assembled automatically from reporting by The Guardian Australia, Stuff and ABC News Australia. Follow the source links below for the full coverage.
